_readme: Single source of truth for CHANNEL STATE and DECISION DATES.
Written 31 Jul 2026 after the Boris Cherny / YC talk 'Delete Your CLAUDE.md'.
Rule: anything that CHANGES lives here. Prose files (OPERATING-NOTES) keep only
timeless, counterintuitive lessons. Task prompts must READ this, never restate it.
Why: on 30-31 Jul the same fact (IG paused, TikTok paused, Meta token revoked) was
copied into 4+ task prompts and 2 python files. When TikTok was dropped, post_guard
and the daily card still asked for it -- the exact drift that caused the 4-day
blackout, just in a different file. One fact, one place.

kind = which pipeline a channel belongs to. Added 31 Jul after a dry-run of the daily card rule (state != paused AND auto == false) pulled PANTIP into the VIDEO card - pantip is a forum-comment flow with its own approval path, not a clip upload. Selection rules must filter on kind, never on state alone.

publication_control.false_capability_note: automation_capable=false means no currently verified automation route is recorded here; it is not a permanent claim about the channel.

Recording it rather than re-arguing it: pantip is state=limited under a FINAL WARNING where a repeat offence is a permanent ban, and it is simultaneously the highest-value channel in the system (4 affiliate clicks from 14 sessions, the only channel producing any conversion event at all). It is the one channel where a mistake cannot be undone. The owner owns this call; this note exists so that if it ever goes wrong the reasoning is legible rather than reconstructed.

That reasoning was faulty: the revocation applies to THIS project's app, not to a separate platform with its own integrations. Capability of an unexamined tool was inferred from facts about our own account. The correct move was to test what the bot can actually reach, not to assert a limit.

decides: posts per day per channel (1 or 2)
gates.note: Two rules disagree and both are live. POSTING-POLICY_antispam_20260702.md rule 2 says <=2/day/channel; STANDING-RULE_autopost.md (18 Jul, owner instruction, and until 31 Jul NOT even committed to git) says 1/day/channel. For Threads the owner then approved 2/day explicitly on 19 Jul, which post-dates the standing rule - so 2 clearly governs there. For Facebook nothing resolves it: the live guard (fb-evening-safetynet) enforces 2. policy.limits.posts_per_day.default is therefore set to 2 = what the system actually enforces today, NOT a ruling. Found 31 Jul 2026 while auditing my own breach of 3 FB posts in 20 minutes - which is over BOTH caps either way.
gates.decision: cap stays 2/day/channel; the >=3h gap is the real anti-blast guard
gates.rationale: Three things point the same way. (1) POSTING-POLICY_antispam is the document comply_gate/qa_gate are meant to enforce, and it says 2. (2) The owner explicitly approved Threads 2/day on 19 Jul, which POST-DATES the 18 Jul standing rule - so the standing rule was already being refined per-channel rather than held at 1. (3) The standing rule's own stated purpose was 'กัน shadowban - ห้าม blast'; blasting is spacing, not volume. 3 posts in 20 minutes (31 Jul) breaks the spacing rule even at a cap of 1, and 2 posts 6h apart breaks nothing. REVERSIBLE: set limits.posts_per_day.default to 1 and this becomes the stricter rule again, no code change needed.

Worse, the sales page carries zero Gumroad links - the only checkout offered is 'add a stranger on LINE', and LINE friends = 1. This gate exists so the next reading is taken against a threshold set BEFORE the data arrives.
preconditions: A0 (BLOCKING, owner): the 10-page PDF must exist and be uploaded as its own Gumroad product. Until it does, the page is taking orders it cannot fill.

internal_traffic._why: GA4 internal-traffic matching requires private network values. The public policy stores only this fail-closed contract; live egress state and configured CIDRs stay in ignored local runtime files.

internal_traffic.verified_how: Verify the private CIDRs in GA4 Admin and keep public logs free of network addresses.
internal_traffic.on_mismatch: Treat every GA4 decision as UNTRUSTED until the private egress state is covered by the private CIDR list. Never widen a consumer network range to hide address rotation.

clicktest_isolation._why: Two different populations needed two different fixes and neither one covers the other. clicktest looks like a bot to GA4, so the IP rule was never what protected it; real-Chrome automation does not look like a bot, so source-side opt-out in clicktest was never what protected that. Writing this down because the next reader will otherwise assume one fix was enough.
clicktest_isolation.mechanism: ga-disable-<GA4_ID>=true injected before page scripts, plus traffic_type=internal
clicktest_isolation.self_check: The run counts its own requests to */collect and FAILs if any escape, so the one-time manual proof (1 -> 0) is re-proved on every run. Reverse-tested 1 Aug: opt-out on = 0 hits, opt-out removed = 2 hits.

task_roots._finding: Folder presence is not execution authority. The current guard reads stable snapshots of both Claude Desktop scheduled-tasks registries and binds each record to its exact prompt root. Cowork has 11 orphan folders and CCD has 1; enabled state comes only from the registries.
task_roots._why_it_matters: A byte-identical mirror can be unreachable, while an enabled registry may point to a retired no-op prompt. Content equality therefore cannot prove execution ownership. Registry state, prompt retirement state, role capabilities and executable side effects must be checked together.
task_roots.rule: Before editing a task prompt, read the stable scheduler ownership export from tools/automation_policy_guard.py --registry-json. Never infer ownership from a folder and never edit scheduler registry JSON by hand.
task_roots.guarded_by: tools/automation_policy_guard.py plus preflight automation ownership gate; cowork-task-watchdog is read-only evidence review and is not authority to mutate a scheduler.
